g.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to June 2026. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Dashed rule: no difference. Each row is the error of the full set (G9) without the variables that one group adds, minus the error of the full set. Error: mean absolute error. Positive means the group helped. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before. G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation. G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation. G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables. G10: G9 plus CAMS aerosol. Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'

text.font-family: Matter XH, DM Sans, sans-serif
text.tspan: Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to June 2026. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS:
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months.
Dashed rule: no difference. Each row is the error of the full set (G9) without the
variables that one group adds, minus the error of the full set. Error: mean absolute
error. Positive means the group helped.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar
radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before.
G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation.
G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation.
G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables.
Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
